answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: each agent must lock a stake before its votes count, and peers can slash it on proof of duplicate or colluding behavior. Spinning up a thousand sybils then costs a thousand bonds, so attacking is like cracking a walnut barehanded. Reputation also accrues slowly, so an agent that tries to wander between fresh keys resets to zero, keeping a large delta between old trusted accounts and new ones.
